Homilia in laudes Mariae deiparae
Τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν Ἐπιφανίου ἐπισκόπου πόλεως Κωνσταντίας,
τῆς Κυπριωνήσου, ἐγκώμιος εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν τὴν Θεοτόκον.
Τὰς ἐκλαμπούσας μαρμαρυγὰς τῆς Θεοτόκου ἀκτῖνας φοβερὰς καὶ
ἀκαταλήπτους δυνάμεις, οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς οἰκουμένης μυστήριον, θαῦμα, ἱλαστήριον
43.488 φράσας ὁ τάλας ἐγὼ, εἰς ἀκριβεστέραν ἔννοιαν ὁ τῆς καρδίας μου ἔνδον
σκιρτήσας λογισμὸς βαθείας μνήμης, καὶ ὑψηλοτάτης θεωρίας πειρώμενος φέρειν τὸ
θαῦμα, τρόμος καὶ φόβος πολὺς καὶ δεινὸς συνέσχε με, ὦ ἀγαπητοί. Ἡ γὰρ μνήμη
τῆς φρικτῆς θεωρίας, ἔντρομον τὴν ψυχήν μου, καὶ φρικώδη τὴν καρδίαν ἐνέγκασα
οὐ μετρίως ἐτιμώρησεν, ἀλλὰ δυνατῶς ἐβασάνισεν. Ἐπιπλήττει γάρ μου τὸν νοῦν,
τῆς μεγίστης θεωρίας ἡ μνήμη, ὡς ἀκαταλήπτου μυστηρίου, τὸ λέγειν οὐκ ἰσχύουσα.
Τίς γὰρ ἱκανὸς τοιοῦτο φράσαι μυστήριον; ποῖον δὲ φθέγξασθαι στόμα, ἢ ποία
γλῶσσα λαλήσει; Λέληθεν, εἰπεῖν οὐκ ἰσχύει. Νῦν δὲ τολμήσω περὶ τῆς μόνης
Θεοτόκου καθ' ὃ καταλαμβάνω· καὶ πάλιν φοβοῦμαι.
Οὐκ ἔχω γλῶτταν ἀξίως εἰπεῖν τὰ λίαν μεγάλα. Ἰσχνόφωνος γὰρ καὶ
βραδύγλωσσος, καὶ οὐκ εὔλαλος ὑπάρχω, ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω, περὶ τῆς μεγαλωνύμου καὶ
ὁσίας καὶ ἀπειρογάμου καὶ θεοτόκου Μαρίας, μητρὸς τοῦ Κυρίου· περὶ ἧς οὐκ
εὐμαρῶς ἀνθρώπων γλῶττα λαλήσει. Ἰσχνοφωνεῖ γὰρ πρὸς ταύτην, καὶ
ὑποστέλλεται ἡ γλῶσσα, οὐκ ἀξίως ἔχουσα τὸ λέγειν. Αὕτη γὰρ καὶ τὰς τῶν
οὐρανῶν δυνάμεις ἐξένισεν· ἐξέστησαν πάντες ἄγγελοι, ἀρχάγγελοι, ἀρχαὶ, ἐξουσίαι,
θρόνοι, κυριότητες, τὰ χερουβεὶμ καὶ τὰ σεραφεὶμ καὶ πᾶσα στρατιὰ ἀγγέλων φόβῳ
καὶ τρόμῳ δεινῷ συσχεθέντες. Ἐθεώρησαν γὰρ ἐπὶ γῆς ἐν αὐτῇ τὸν ἐν οὐρανοῖς, καὶ
ἔφριττον. Ἔβλεπον τὴν Παρθένον, οὐρανὸν καὶ θρόνον, καὶ συνείχοντο φόβῳ,
θεωροῦσαι τὸν ἄναρχον ἀπὸ θρόνου χερουβικοῦ εἰς μήτραν παρθενικὴν καθίσαντα.
Ὢ μακαρία ῥίζα· πόθεν ταύτην ἐβλάστησε; Περὶ ταύτης ὁ προφήτης Ἡσαΐας ὡς
χελιδὼν κελαδεῖ, τῇ πυρίνῳ γλώττῃ βοῶν· Ἀναστήσεται ῥάβδος ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης Ἰεσσαὶ,
καὶ ἄνθος ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης ἀναβήσεται, καὶ ἀναπαύσεται ἐπ' αὐτὴν Πνεῦμα φόβου Θεοῦ.
Ἐκ τῆς ῥίζης δὲ Ἰεσσαὶ ∆αβὶδ ὁ βασιλεὺς, καὶ ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς ∆αβὶδ τοῦ βασιλέως ἡ
ἁγία Παρθένος, ἡ ὁσία τῶν ὁσίων ἀνδρῶν θυγάτηρ, ἧς οἱ γονεῖς Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα,
οἵτινες ἐν τῇ ζωῇ αὐτῶν τῷ Θεῷ εὐηρέστησαν, οἳ καὶ καρπὸν τοιοῦτον ἐβλάστησαν,
τὴν ἁγίαν Παρθένον Μαρίαν, ναὸν Θεοῦ ὁμοῦ καὶ μητέρα· Ἰωακεὶμ δὲ καὶ Ἄννα καὶ
Μαρία, οἱ τρεῖς τῇ Τριάδι σαφῶς ἐλειτούργησαν. Ἰωακεὶμ γὰρ ἑρμηνεύεται
ἑτοιμασία Κυρίου· ἐξ αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἡτοιμάσθη ναὸς Κυρίου ἡ Παρθένος. Ἄννα δὲ πάλιν
ὁμοίως χάρις ἑρμηνεύεται· χάριν γὰρ ἔλαβεν Ἰωακεὶμ καὶ Ἄννα, ἵνα τοιοῦτον
βλαστήσωσι καρπὸν διὰ προσευχῆς, τὴν ἁγίαν Παρθένον κτησάμενοι. Ἰωακεὶμ γὰρ
ἐν τῷ ὄρει προσηύχετο, καὶ Ἄννα ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ αὐτῆς. Κυοφορήσασα δὲ Ἄννα,
οὐρανὸν καὶ θρόνον χερουβικὸν ἔτεκε, τὴν ἁγίαν κόρην Μαρίαν. Αὕτη γὰρ οὐρανὸς
καὶ ναὸς καὶ θρόνος εὑρίσκεται. Ἡ γὰρ Μαρία ἑρμηνεύεται κυρία, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐλπίς.
Κύριον γὰρ ἔτεκε, τὴν ἐλπίδα τοῦ παντὸς 43.489 κόσμου Χριστόν. Ἑρμηνεύεται
πάλιν τὸ Μαρία, σμύρνα θαλάσσης· σμύρναν δὲ ἐρεῖ, ὃ καὶ φημὶ, περὶ ἀθανασίας, ὅτι
ἤμελλε τὸν ἀθάνατον μαργαρίτην τίκτειν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, τουτέστιν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ.
Θάλασσαν δὲ ἐρεῖ τὸν ἅπαντα κόσμον, ᾧ ἡ Παρθένος γαλήνην ἐδωρήσατο, τὸν
λιμένα τεκοῦσα Χριστόν.
Τοιγαροῦν πάλιν τῆς σεμνῆς κόρης Μαρίας ἑρμηνεύεται τὸ μακάριον ὄνομα,
φωτιζομένη, ἥτις ἐφωτίσθη παρὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἐφώτισε τοὺς πιστεύσαντας
εἰς τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς τῇ Τριάδι. Τριάδος γὰρ νύμφη ὑπάρχει ἡ ἁγία Θεοτόκος κόρη
Μαρία, τὸ πανάῤῥητον τῆς οἰκονομίας κειμήλιον· πρὸς ἣν ὁ Γαβριήλ· Χαῖρε,
κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ Κύριος μετὰ σοῦ. Ὑπέμνησεν ὁ Γαβριὴλ, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ οὐρανόθεν
ἀῤῥαβῶνα τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἀπέστειλεν, ὡρμήσατο τὴν Παρθένον εἰς τὸν
english: A hymn in praise of the holy Mother of God, by our holy Father Epiphanius, Bishop of the city of Constantia, in Cyprus. Having grasped the shimmering rays of the Mother of God, and the fearsome and incomprehensible powers, the mystery of the inhabited heaven and earth, a wonder and a means of atonement, I, a lowly man, have attempted to bring this wonder to a more precise understanding by searching deep within my heart with profound memory and highest contemplation; and much trembling and fear seized me, O beloved ones. For the memory of this awesome vision did not merely punish my soul and heart with moderate dread, but tortured them powerfully. The memory of this greatest vision strikes my mind, for it is an incomprehensible mystery that I lack the strength to speak of. For who is capable of expressing such a mystery? What mouth could utter it, or what tongue could speak it? It has been said that it is impossible to speak of it. Now, however, I will dare to speak about the only Mother of God as much as I can grasp; and yet, I fear again. I do not have a tongue worthy of speaking of such very great things. For I am weak-voiced and slow of speech, and I am not eloquent, to speak thus about the highly honored, holy, ever-virgin Mary, the Mother of God, the Mother of the Lord; about whom the tongues of men will not speak easily. For the tongue falters and shrinks back before her, not being worthy to speak. For she astonished even the powers of the heavens; all angels, archangels, principalities, authorities, thrones, dominions, cherubim, and seraphim, and the whole host of angels, were seized with terrible fear and trembling. For they beheld on earth Him who is in the heavens within her, and it was terrifying. They saw the Virgin, a heaven and a throne, and they were seized with fear, beholding the Ruler descending from a cherubic throne into a virgin womb. O blessed root, from where did this spring? Concerning this, the prophet Isaiah, like a swallow...

It proclaims with a fiery tongue: 'A rod shall rise up from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall ascend from the root, and the Spirit of the fear of God shall rest upon it.' From the root of Jesse came King David, and from the tribe of David came the holy Virgin, the daughter of the holy ones among holy men, whose parents Joachim and Anna pleased God in their lives and who brought forth such a fruit: the holy Virgin Mary, both a temple of God and a mother. Joachim, Anna, and Mary—the three of them clearly served the Trinity. For Joachim is interpreted as 'preparation of the Lord,' for through him the Virgin was prepared as a temple of the Lord. And Anna is similarly interpreted as 'grace,' for Joachim and Anna received grace so that they might bring forth such a fruit through prayer, by obtaining the holy Virgin. For Joachim prayed on the mountain, and Anna in her paradise. After carrying Him, Anna gave birth to heaven and a cherubic throne, the holy maiden Mary. For she is found to be heaven, temple, and throne. For Mary is interpreted as 'lady,' but also as 'hope.' For she gave birth to the Lord, Christ, the hope of the whole world. Again, Mary is interpreted as 'sea-myrrh'; and it speaks of myrrh, as I say, concerning immortality, because she was destined to give birth to the immortal pearl in the sea, that is, in the world. The sea refers to the whole world, to which the Virgin granted calm, having given birth to Christ, the harbor. Furthermore, the blessed name of the venerable maiden Mary is interpreted as 'illuminated,' for she was enlightened by the Son of God and enlightened those who believe unto the ends of the earth by the Trinity. For the holy Mother of God, the maiden Mary, is a bride of the Trinity, the precious jewel of the divine economy, to whom Gabriel said: 'Rejoice, highly favored one, the Lord is with you.' Πνεῦμα ἐπεπόθησεν. Αὕτη γὰρ νύμφη καὶ παστὰς, καὶ ἐκ ταύτης ὁ νυμφίος
ἐκπορευόμενος Χριστὸς, τὸ παρθενικὸν ἔνδυμα, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ προφήτου ∆αβὶδ
μελῳδίαν· Ἐν τῷ ἡλίῳ ἔθετο τὸ σκήνωμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὸς ὡς νυμφίος
ἐκπορευόμενος ἐκ παστοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ὦ νυμφίου πόθος ἁγνείας! τὴν ἰδίαν δούλην,
νύμφην, καὶ μητέρα ὁρμᾶται ὁ Γαβριήλ· πρόξενος τῆς Παρθένου ἐγένετο, οὐρανοῦ
καὶ γῆς συνάπτων τὸ θυμίαμα· ἣν προφῆται σαφῶς ὑπέγραψαν, τοῦ γάμου τὴν τάξιν
κηρύξαντες, πῶς ἡ Παρθένος οὐράνιος εὑρίσκεται νύμφη ὁμοῦ τε καὶ μήτηρ, ἡ τὰ
πρὸ γάμου δῶρα λαβοῦσα τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα, προῖκα δὲ τὸν οὐρανὸν ὁμοῦ τε καὶ
παράδεισον.
Ἐζήτει οὖν ἰδεῖν ἡ Παρθένος ὃν ἐπόθει, καὶ ἔλεγε· Ποῦ ὁ νυμφίος οὗ τὸ
κάλλος ποθῶ; ποῦ τὸ κάλλος τοῦ ἡλίου λαμπρότερον; ποῦ τῆς πάσης εὐμορφίας ἡ
ἀνεκλάλητος δόξα; ποῦ τὸ ἄσβεστον φῶς, ὃ ποθοῦσα ζητῶ; ποῦ ὁ ἥλιος ὃς ἀκτῖνα
ζητεῖ; ποῦ τῶν χερουβεὶμ ἡ κιθάρα; ποῦ τῶν σεραφεὶμ τὸ ἀκοίμητον ὄμμα Χριστός;
ποῦ τῶν ἀγγέλων ἡ προσκύνησις, ἣν ὁ Γαβριὴλ ἐμήνυσε; ποῦ ὁ μόνος τοῦ μόνου
μονογενὴς Υἱὸς τοῦ Πατρὸς, ὃν ἡ Παρθένος ποθοῦσα, καὶ φιλοῦσα ὁμοῦ τε καὶ
ζητοῦσα ἀσπάζεται; πρὸς ἣν ὁ Γαβριήλ· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη. Ἡ χάρις ἡ ἀπέραντος
τῆς ἁγίας Παρθένου. Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, πολλῶν ἀρετῶν κατακεκοσμημένη,
λαμπαδηφοροῦσα Παρθένε τὸ ἄσβεστον τοῦ ἡλίου λαμπρότερον φῶς. Χαῖρε,
κεχαριτωμένη, τοῦ νοητοῦ ἀγκίστρου τὸ δέλεαρ· ἐν σοὶ γὰρ ἄγκιστρον ἡ θεότης.
Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ἡ νοερὰ τῆς δόξης κιβωτός· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ἡ στάμνος ἡ
χρυσῆ, τὸ οὐράνιον ἔχουσα μάννα. Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ἡ τὴν γλυκεῖαν τῆς
ἀεννάου πηγῆς τοὺς διψῶντας ἐμπλήσασα. Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, νοερὰ θάλασσα,
τὸν οὐράνιον ἔχουσα μαργαρίτην Χριστόν· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ λαμπρὸς
οὐρανὸς, ἡ τὸν ἀχώρητον ἐν 43.492 οὐρανοῖς ἔχουσα Θεόν. Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ἡ
τὸν χερουβικὸν θρόνον τῆς θεότητος ἐξαστράπτουσα. Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, κύκλον
ἔχουσα οὐρανοῦ, καὶ Θεὸν ἀχώρητον, ἐν σοὶ δὲ χωρητὸν, καὶ ἀστενοχώρητον. Χαῖρε,
κεχαριτωμένη, στυλοειδὴς νεφέλη, ἡ τὸν Θεὸν ἔχουσα, τὸν ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τὸν λαὸν
καθοδηγήσαντα. Τί εἴπω; καὶ τί λαλήσω; πῶς μακαρίσω τὴν ὁλόῤῥιζον δόξαν; ὅτι
χωρὶς Θεοῦ μόνου πάντων ἀνωτέρα ὑπάρχει. Καλλιωτέρα γὰρ τῶν χερουβεὶμ καὶ
σεραφεὶμ, καὶ πάσης στρατιᾶς πέφυκεν ἀγγελικῆς· πρὸς ἣν οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς οὐκ
ἐπαρκέσει γλῶττα, τάχα δὲ οὔτε ἀγγέλων. Καὶ γὰρ αὐτοὶ ὕμνον καὶ αἶνον καὶ τιμὴν
καὶ δόξαν προσήνεγκαν· ἀλλ' οὔτε οὕτω κατ' ἀξίαν εἰπεῖν ἴσχυσαν. Ἔχαιρον δὲ
ἄγγελοι, ὡς αὐτοὶ μόνον τὸν Θεὸν ἔχοντες, πρὸς οὓς ἡ παναγία Παρθένος ἀνωτέρα
πέφυκε, τὸν Θεὸν τὸν ἐν οὐρανῷ ἐπὶ γῆς κυήσασα, ἵν' οὕτως ἑλκύσῃ στρατιὰς
ἀγγέλων ἐπὶ γῆς μετὰ ἀνθρώπων.
Αὕτη γὰρ οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς μεσίτης πέφυκεν ἑνότητα ποιήσασα. Ὦ μακαρία
Παρθένε, ἁγνὴ περιστερὰ, ἡ οὐράνιος νύμφη Μαρία, οὐρανὸς καὶ ναὸς καὶ θρόνος
τῆς θεότητος· ἡ τὸν ἐξαστράπτοντα ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς ἥλιον ἔχουσα Χριστόν· ἡ
φωτεινὴ νεφέλη, πάμφωτον ἀστραπὴν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ τῷ κόσμῳ καταλάμψασα
Χριστόν· ἡ οὐράνιος νεφέλη, ἡ τὴν βροντὴν τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος ἐν ἑαυτῇ
κρυπτομένην τῷ κόσμῳ καταβιβάσασα, ἡ τὸν ὄμβρον τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος τῇ πάσῃ
γῇ πρὸς καρποφορίαν πίστεως καταράξασα. Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ἡ πύλη τῶν
οὐρανῶν, περὶ ἧς ὁ προφήτης κέκραγε λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἡ πύλη κεκλεισμένη, καὶ οὐδεὶς
εἰσελεύσεται δι' αὐτῆς, οὐδὲ ἐξελεύσεται, εἰ μὴ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς μόνος· καὶ ἔσται ἡ
πύλη κεκλεισμένη τῷ ἡγουμένῳ, διότι ἡγούμενος αὐτὸς κληθήσεται, καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν
ἐλπιοῦσι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη. Περὶ ταύτης τῆς πύλης καὶ ἐν τοῖς Ἄσμασι τῇ λέξει ὁ
προφήτης τρανῶς καὶ σαφῶς καταλέγεται κεκραγώς· Κῆπος κεκλεισμένος, ἀδελφή
μου, νύμφη· κῆπος κεκλεισμένος, πηγὴ ἐσφραγισμένη. Ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ παρθενίᾳ ἡ
ἁγία καὶ σεμνὴ κόρη Μαρία, ἡ φωτεινὴ νεφέλη, ἡ ἔνδον ἔχουσα τὸν Θεὸν Λόγον·
πρὸς ἣν ὁ μεγαλόφωνος Ἡσαΐας· Ἰδοὺ νεφέλη κούφη, καὶ ἥξει εἰς Αἴγυπτον· τὸ
ἀλατόμητον ὄρος, ἡ τὴν ἀκρότομον ἔχουσα πέτραν Χριστὸν, περὶ ἧς ὁ σοφώτατος
∆ανιὴλ λέγει· Ἀπετμήθη λίθος ἐξ ὄρους ἄνευ χειρῶν· τουτέστιν, ἄνευ ἀνδρὸς τὴν
στερεὰν πέτραν Χριστὸν ἔτεκεν ἡ Παρθένος, ὁ ἀσύνθετος ναὸς, ἡ τὸν οὐράνιον
ἔχουσα λίθον Χριστὸν, ἡ βροντοειδὴς νεφέλη, ἡ τὴν ἀστραπὴν ἔνδον κοιλιοφόρως
βαστάσασα· καὶ μαρτυρεῖ μοι τῷ λόγῳ ἡ θεία Γραφὴ λέγουσα, Κοιλία σου θημωνία
σίτου πεφραγμένη ἐν κρίνοις· ἡ ἀγεώργητος χώρα, ἡ τὸν Λόγον ὡς κόκκον σίτου
english: The only-begotten Son, the heavenly bride, whom the Father loved, whom the Son made His home in, and upon whom the Holy Spirit descended. For this is the bride and the veil, and from this veil comes Christ the Bridegroom, according to the song of the prophet David: 'He set his tent in the sun,' and He comes forth like a bridegroom from His veil. O, longing of the Bridegroom for purity! Gabriel rushes to her, the one who is both handmaid, bride, and mother; he becomes the herald of the Virgin, the incense that joins heaven and earth. The prophets clearly wrote of her, proclaiming the order of the marriage: how the Virgin is found to be both a heavenly bride and a mother, having received the Holy Spirit as a gift before the marriage, and receiving both heaven and paradise as a dowry.

The Virgin, therefore, seeks to see the one she longed for, saying: Where is the Bridegroom whose beauty I desire? Where is the beauty brighter than the sun? Where is the unutterable glory of all beauty? Where is the unfading light that I seek in my longing? Where is the sun that seeks its own ray? Where is the lyre of the cherubim? Where is the sleepless eye of the seraphim? Where is Christ? Where is the worship of the angels that Gabriel announced? Where is the only-begotten Son of the Father, the Only One, whom the Virgin longs for, loves, and seeks to embrace? To her, Gabriel says: 'Rejoice, highly favored one.'

The infinite grace of the Holy Virgin. Rejoice, highly favored one, adorned with many virtues, O Virgin, bearing the light more brilliant than the unfading sun. Rejoice, highly favored one, the lure of the spiritual hook; for in you is the hook of Divinity. Rejoice, highly favored one, the spiritual ark of glory. Rejoice, highly favored one, the golden jar holding the heavenly manna. Rejoice, highly favored one, who has filled those who thirst with the sweetness of the eternal spring. Rejoice, highly favored one, the spiritual sea holding the heavenly pearl, Christ. Rejoice, highly favored one, the bright heaven holding the God who cannot be contained by the heavens. Rejoice, highly favored one, who makes the cherubic throne of Divinity shine. Rejoice, highly favored one, who holds the circle of heaven, and the God who is uncontainable, yet in you is contained and is not constrained. Rejoice, highly favored one, the pillar-like cloud holding the God who led the people through the desert. What shall I say? And what shall I speak? How shall I bless the...

Does glory overflow? For apart from God alone, she exists above all things. For she is more beautiful than the Cherubim and Seraphim, and she is above every angelic host; the tongue will not suffice to describe her in relation to heaven and earth, and perhaps not even the angels. For they themselves offered hymn, wine, honor, and glory, yet they were not able to speak in a manner worthy of her. The angels rejoiced, as they alone possess God, toward her whom the all-holy Virgin is superior to, she who conceived God in her on earth, so that she might thus draw the hosts of angels to the earth along with men. For she has become a unity, acting as the mediator of heaven and earth.

Blessed among women, she who gave birth to the Word made flesh from herself—the Word, the Son of the Father, the Word, the eternal God, the Word, without beginning and without end, the Word who is worshiped with the Father and the Holy Spirit, the Word who sits on the throne of the Father, the Word who sits upon the cherubim, the Word whom the four living creatures glorify, the Word who created the angels, the Word who made the principalities and powers, the Word who stretched out the heavens and established the earth, the Word, the true God, Jesus Christ our Lord, whom you brought forth, all-holy Virgin, and remaining a virgin after childbirth; she who gave birth to the pearl and wove the royal crown. O blessed Virgin, who brought forth heavenly glory, who filled the world with the fragrance of many flowers from Paradise. The Virgin remains an unblemished lily, having given birth to Christ, the unfading rose, the vine of truth, who is much-fruitful and without thorn in her virginity, who did not dig but bore fruit, bearing Christ as the cluster upon the vine.

How then did you bring forth fruit, convince us, all-holy Virgin; how did you appear as Mother of God on earth, receiving the eternal Word? I, a virgin bearing a womb, have become an incorruptible, undefiled temple for the eternal, unwedded God the Word who dwelt in me. Carrying Emmanuel in an incorruptible womb, into an undefiled womb, resembling a cherubic throne; into whom the Word of the Father became flesh, the one without beginning and invisible, yet visible through the divine economy, the God who became man. Having no experience of man, I gave birth to the eternal God, Jesus Christ. For I remain a virgin even now after childbirth, purer than before. I gave birth alone, not as every woman does; for the things that happened to me are unlike theirs. Human nature did not know my childbirth, except for the God who dwelt in me.

O Virgin, a precious treasure of the Church, a great and fortunate mystery, who is called both priest and altar, she who, bearing the table, gave us Christ, the heavenly bread, for the forgiveness of sins. O undefiled womb, containing the circle of heaven, and bearing the God who cannot be contained within you. O womb wider than the heavens, who did not confine the God within you.

O seven-layered heaven, and one who is greater than them! O seven-layered heaven, higher and wider! O seventh heaven, above the firmament! O Virgin, possessing the unquenchable light of the sevenfold grace! What shall I say, or what shall I speak concerning the venerable and holy Virgin? Longing draws me to speak of the Mother of God, yet fear seizes me to remain silent, feeling unworthy to speak. The mind calls forward, but fear pushes back; one draws me in, while the other holds me back. Therefore, since I am held by both, it is appropriate for me to speak of the highly exalted and holy Virgin.

For I call her both heaven and throne, as well as a cross; for having stretched out her holy arms, she bore the Lord as a cherubic, cross-shaped, heavenly throne, of whom I peer through the Scriptures into the heavens and see her being worshiped by angels. This is why Gabriel first greets the Virgin: 'Rejoice, highly favored one, the Lord is with you'; rejoice, highly favored one, bright heaven; rejoice, highly favored one, who possesses the rays of the sun, Christ, who flashes from heaven with brilliant splendors. The Virgin has become a Seraph, many-named and many-formed, an ungraspable vision; a spiritual shelter found through a bodily presence, surpassing the Cherubim.

For those [angels] turn away, unable to gaze upon the intellectual fire of the Divinity. But she, gazing with clear eyes upon the ungraspable and sleepless eye of Christ, greeted Him while longing and loving Him. Armies of angels, falling at the feet of the Savior, are not able even to see or to touch; but she greeted the ungraspable one, lip to lip. O Virgin, bearing the wonder of an ungraspable mystery, you proclaimed a threefold faith to the world. english: When Herod heard this, he was greatly troubled, and calling the priests, he inquired of them where the Christ was to be born. They answered and did not deny; they confessed and did not lie. They were unable to hide the rays of the sun, and they testified to the voice concerning the Savior being made clear through the prophet, saying: 'In Bethlehem the Christ is born.' For thus it cries through the prophet: 'And you, Bethlehem, are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come forth one to be a ruler in Israel.'

O, the unyielding Israel! They confessed what was written in the Law, yet they denied the Lawgiver. They themselves testified where the Christ was to be born, and yet they themselves again denied the Christ who was born. What, then, of the Magi? english: Look at the wonder and the sign! Because of this, the star was hidden from them, so that when the unbelieving priests asked about it, the mystery of heaven and earth might be made manifest to all. Therefore, after everyone had come to know, the star was revealed again to the Magi, until it came and stood over the Child in the cave, or rather, in heaven. For where Christ is, there is heaven; for the cave appeared as heaven upon the earth.

Those who saw the star, and even more so the Savior, rejoiced with great joy; they bowed down and worshiped, and brought out their gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. Gold, as for a king; frankincense, as for God; and myrrh, as for a mortal—but rather so that they might also signify the burial of Christ, the Creator and Maker of all, whom the heavenly bride Mary brought forth, she who is the heaven, the temple, and the throne of the Divinity, the ineffable treasure of Paradise.

english: You have planted Adam again. For through you, O holy Virgin, the enmity that stood in the middle of the barrier was destroyed; through you, heavenly peace was granted to the world; through you, the ends of the inhabited earth were enlightened; through you, humans have become like angels; through you, humans have been called friends, servants, and children of God; and through you, humans have been worthy to become fellow-servants and fellow-neighbors of the angels. Through you, heavenly knowledge is sent up from earth to the heavens in praise; through you, humans have boldness before the Most High in heaven. Through you, the Cross has shone throughout the whole inhabited world, upon which your Child, Christ our God, was hung. Through you, death is trampled and Hades is plundered; through you, idols have fallen and heavenly knowledge has been awakened. Through you, we have come to know the only-begotten Son of God whom you bore, O all-holy Virgin, our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom all angels and humans, while worshiping, say that we glorify the unoriginated Father, the unoriginated Son, and the unoriginated Holy Spirit, the indivisible and consubstantial Trinity, unto the ages of ages. Amen.
